summary: BLM lookout on Big Southern Butte near Atomic City, Idaho: built 1963, last staffed 2004, removed 2013; the summit road is still maintained.

facts.design: Two-story cab with slanted windows on a concrete structure
facts.agency: Department of the Interior, Bureau of Land Management (Idaho Falls District)
facts.status_note: Removed in 2013 per sources; a 2021 guide says the BLM still maintains the access road, probably for electronic installations at the summit

access.note: Road from a BLM gate, closed by the BLM in winter and hiked by many people; a large section of the land north of the butte is Idaho National Laboratory land and is closed to the public

events.note: Temporary lookout arrangements made while a modern lookout was planned
Concrete structure with an observation cab completed; two-story cab with slanted windows
Air tankers dropped retardant to protect the lookout; the source does not name the fire
Lookout building and related structures removed; gone by summer 2013

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register gives 7,523 ft (2,293 m) for the site. Idaho Fire Lookouts gives 7,560 ft, and the climbing guide gives 7,560 ft as the height of the butte. The register figure is kept.

notes_for_editor: Brief's build year 1963, removal 2013 and FFLOS registration (March 25, 2020) are confirmed. Today's condition is unverified: the 2021 climbing guide mentions the road and probable electronic installations at the summit but not any lookout remains, and the BLM visit page it links was not read. Elevation disagrees across sources (7,523 ft register vs 7,560 ft Idaho Fire Lookouts); the register figure is kept. The 1962 newspaper quotes are read through Rex's page, a secondary copy. No photos added: the register's 2012 photo has no image URL in the crawl text.
